content.text:
## What I found

The final head `f1ead20` fixes the money domain and the token-mechanism gap as claimed: all twelve command criteria passed at that commit on recorded evidence, F1–F7 and F9–F13 are resolved, and F8's non-fix is defensible. But the last rework's fix for the architecture scan (F3/F10) strips comments without modelling string literals, which **silently hides a real forbidden dependency** — I proved a `require('../store/memoryStore')` in `src/users/routes.js` goes green when bracketed by the string literals `'/*'` and `'*/'`, or placed after a string containing `//`, while the identical require is red without them.

## Why it matters

The branch's only architectural enforcement can now pass over the exact edge it exists to stop, and the trigger is ordinary code (a glob such as `'orders/*'`, a protocol-relative URL) rather than an attack; there is no CI and no negative control, so the loss would never be noticed. Acting means one rule-level change — strip string literals before comments — which also closes the remaining false-fail; not acting leaves a gate whose declared scope ("comments are stripped") is wider than its effective scope.

## Do this first

1. Escalate the major finding **N1** to the human with the fix `test/architecture.test.js:41-45` — blank quoted literals before stripping comments — and re-run `node --test test/architecture.test.js` plus the two planted controls below; the rework budget is spent, so this is a human decision, not another cycle.
2. Record **N2** (three PR.md claims still outrun the implementation) as `related_to: F1, F2, F11` — this is the third consecutive round with a claim-accuracy finding, which is the convergence signal the ledger gate reads.
3. Record **N3/N4/N5** as minor, and decide `accepted-risk` or a follow-up for the top-of-range money band.

## What I did not check

- Timing behaviour of `timingSafeEqual` (no oracle exists; PR.md discloses this) — closes only with a measurement harness nobody has.
- The construction-time provider `TypeError` (`src/payments/service.js:8`) has no test; closes with `node --test` on a new case asserting `createPaymentService({store, orders, provider: {}})` throws.
- PR.md's planted-revert run ("users 6/7") — I did not reproduce it; the assertion's behaviour is deducible from `test/users.test.js:69-70` with certainty.
- Whether the strengthened `test/money.test.js` oracles still fail at base: `prefix-suite@2325850` was produced with the **8a96e1f** test files (40 tests, no constant-time test), not f1ead20's 41. Closes with `npm test` in a `2325850` worktree holding the head `test/*.js`.

---

## 1. Criteria at `f1ead20`

All twelve: **verified**. Each has a harness record at `f1ead20` with the plan's command, exit 0, and a log showing real execution (nonzero tests, `fail 0`, `skipped 0`, `cancelled 0`).

| Criterion | Verdict | Evidence ID |
|:--|:--|:--|
| AC1-suite / AC8-suite / AC12-suite | verified | `AC1-suite@f1ead20`, `AC8-suite@f1ead20`, `AC12-suite@f1ead20` — `tests 41 / pass 41` |
| AC2-ownership | verified | `AC2-ownership@f1ead20` |
| AC3-reports | verified | `AC3-reports@f1ead20` |
| AC4-money | verified | `AC4-money@f1ead20` |
| AC5-architecture / AC10 / AC14 | verified | `AC5-architecture@f1ead20`, `AC10-architecture@f1ead20`, `AC14-architecture@f1ead20` — `tests 5 / pass 5` |
| AC9-money-bounds / AC13-money-domain | verified | `AC9-money-bounds@f1ead20`, `AC13-money-domain@f1ead20` — `tests 4 / pass 4` |
| AC11-tokens | verified | `AC11-tokens@f1ead20` — `tests 7 / pass 7`, includes "the token signature is compared in constant time" |

Two caveats for the ledger, not verdict changes: the twelve criteria rest on **seven distinct command/commit pairs** (AC1≡AC8≡AC12 and AC5≡AC10≡AC14 are the same evidence by the identity rule), so they are not twelve independent confirmations; and a green `AC14` is weaker than it looks given N1.

My own package criteria: **AC6-review-security verified** — every orders/payments/reports route is `guard.requireUser`/`requireAdmin` (`src/orders/routes.js`, `src/payments/routes.js`, `src/reports/routes.js`), `GET /orders/:id` uses `getOwned`, `orders.get` is no longer exported, `payments.get` checks `userId`, `users.find` returns `toPublic` so `/users/me` leaks no hash, and `REPORT_NAME` (`src/reports/routes.js:13`) is fully anchored and tested before any `path.join`, so no traversal, absolute path or symlink name reaches the filesystem. **AC7-review-regressions verified with a named currency caveat**: `prefix-suite@2325850` maps 13 base failures to defects 1,2,4,5,6,7,8 and the store rule, and no removed symbol (`parseCookies`, `getProvider`/`registerProvider`, `sumLines`/`lineTotal`, exported `get`, exported `toPublic`) has a remaining caller; but that log predates the final `test/money.test.js` and `test/users.test.js`.

## 2. Findings F1–F13

| ID | Verdict | What decides it |
|:--|:--|:--|
| F1 | resolved | PR.md:20,104-114 now claims no behavioural test; `src/auth/tokens.js:25-26` confirms the empty signature returns before the length check and the other three reach it; mechanism test passes (`AC11-tokens@f1ead20`) |
| F2 | resolved | `git show 2325850:src/lib/money.js` — base `isAmount` really used `< 1e-6` on `value*100`, so defect 9 owns the tolerance and defect 7's row no longer misattributes the dust |
| F3 | resolved | scan matches `['"]` both ways and asserts literal args; my step 1 shows the assertion fires (exit 1) |
| F4 | resolved | `src/payments/service.js:8-10` throws at construction; disclosed as unasserted |
| F5 | resolved | `cents >= 1`; `1e-9`, `1e-11`, `0.005` rejected (`AC13-money-domain@f1ead20`) |
| F6 | resolved | `cents <= Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER`; `1e21` and `90071992547409.92` rejected (same log) |
| F7 | resolved | `test/money.test.js:29` reads cents off `toFixed(2)` text — shares no arithmetic with `totalCents` |
| F8 | **not fixed, defensible** | `src/http/router.js:51` (405) and `:59` (400) precede `guard`; README defines no 405, the response is identical for existing and absent resources, and the only disclosure is path existence, which README publishes. Needs `accepted-risk` with `accepted_by: human` |
| F9 | resolved | as F7, plus the negative partition now includes `0.1 + 0.2` and the range boundaries |
| F10 | **partially resolved — open** | comments no longer trip the gate, but a **string** containing `require(name)`/`import(` still fails it (step 1, exit 1), and PR.md:130 claims that case fixed. See N1/N2 |
| F11 | resolved | the "reverting tokens.js would leave the suite green" sentence is gone and is now false |
| F12 | resolved with residual | `70000000000.01` and `700000000000.07` accepted; 0 of 200 000 values in 0.01–2000.00 rejected (step A2). Residual band at 3.5e13–9.0e13: see N4 |
| F13 | resolved | `test/users.test.js:68-70`; any revert removing `crypto.timingSafeEqual(` fails `assert.match`, whatever the comparison's operand order |

## 3. Attack on `fromCents(toCents(v)) === v`

**Accepts nothing README forbids.** The rule accepts `v` only when `v === fl(C/100)` for an in-range integer `C`, i.e. `v` is exactly the canonical double of a two-decimal decimal. `1.234`, `0.005`, `0.125`, `0.1+0.2`, `0.07*3` and `1.1+2.2` are all rejected (step C). The **1-cent floor is exactly right**: the smallest positive two-decimal value is `0.01`, which is accepted, and everything below rounds to 0 cents and is rejected. The **ceiling** rejects two-decimal values above 9.007e13, which README's literal text permits; PR.md discloses that as a product question — fair.

**Rejects values README permits, below the declared ceiling.** `fl(·/100)` stops being injective once cent counts exceed 2^51, so `Math.round(v*100)` can land one cent off the decimal the client sent, and the round trip then fails. Measured: **40 of 700** sampled legal two-decimal amounts in [3.5e13, 9.007e13] are rejected, e.g. `35184372088832.02` → `POST /orders` 400 "unitPrice must be a positive amount with at most two decimals" (**N4**, minor; `src/lib/money.js:16-24`). PR.md:174 says rejection starts "above about 9.007e13" — wrong by a factor of ~2.5.

**Worse in the same band: a reachable order whose stated total can never be paid (N5**, minor; `src/orders/service.js:31-39` + `src/payments/service.js:17`). `unitPrice: 35184372088832.05, quantity: 2` passes `isAmount`, sums to 7036874417766410 cents — a safe integer, so the `Number.isSafeInteger` guard does not fire — and stores `total: 70368744177664.1`. A payment of exactly that total computes `toCents` = 7036874417766409 ≠ 7036874417766410 → 400 forever. That is defect 4's own symptom ("an order that could never be paid at its own stated total") reinstated at the top of the range, and it makes PR.md:30's claim that creation "rejects a summed total that is no longer an exact cent count" incomplete. One-line fix: `if (toCents(fromCents(cents)) !== cents) throw invalid(...)`, or bound the domain at 2^51 cents where the round trip is provably injective. I rate N4/N5 minor on exposure (unit prices of ~3.5e13 currency units); if the human treats the top of the range as in scope — as F6 was — N5 is F6's class and would be major.

**Rejecting `0.1 + 0.2` does not break a legitimate client at plausible magnitudes**, and nothing in 0.01–2000.00 is rejected. Order totals now come from `fromCents`, so a client that echoes back the total it was given always passes. The real change: a client that computes an amount itself by float addition (`0.1+0.1+0.1` → `0.30000000000000004`) now gets 400 where it previously got a silent round to 0.30. README sanctions that (the number has 17 decimals), and failing loud is correct — but it is a client-visible break that PR.md's limitations do not list.

## 4. Attack on the comment stripping and the route selector

**N1 — major — `test/architecture.test.js:41-45`: the stripper does not model string literals, so it hides real dependencies.** `code()` treats any `/*` … `*/` as a comment and any `//` not preceded by `:` as a line comment, wherever they occur.

- `const GLOB = '/*'; const store = require('../store/memoryStore'); const END = '*/';` in `src/users/routes.js` → gate **green, exit 0**, while the identical require without the two string literals is **red, exit 1** (`forbidden dependency: src/users/routes.js -> src/store/memoryStore.js`).
- `const U = '//cdn'; const store = require('../store/memoryStore');` on one line → gate **green, exit 0**.
- A single unmatched `/*` inside a string (a glob such as `'orders/*'`) deletes everything to the next `*/` or to EOF, so **every** require in that file disappears and `every require target exists` passes trivially.
- At head nothing triggers it: the only `//`-in-string in `src/` is `'http://localhost'` (`src/http/router.js:37`), which the `[^:]` guard protects, and no `/*` appears in `src/` at all. The code is correct; the gate protecting it is narrower than PR.md declares. Per `gate-lifecycle` §4 this is an undeclared scope delta → `RESTORE`.
- Code following `*/` on the same line survives (the replacement is per-comment, not per-line), so that attack line finds nothing.

**N2 — minor — the gate can still fail on correct code, and PR.md says it cannot.** `const HINT = 'never use import(x) or require(name) in a message';` in `src/lib/errors.js` → **exit 1**, `src/lib/errors.js has a non-literal require: require(name)`. PR.md:130 lists "a string containing `import(`" among the twelve fixed findings; only the comment case was fixed. Same root cause and same one-line fix as N1 (blank quoted literals, then strip comments). Together with the misstated rejection boundary (N4) and the incomplete defect-8 claim (N5), this is the third consecutive round in which PR.md's claims outrun the code — `related_to: F1, F2, F11`.

**N3 — minor — `test/architecture.test.js:97-98`: the route-module selector misses route modules.** `basename().startsWith('routes.')` gains `.cjs`/`.mjs` and loses the (lowercase-only) `*routes.js` suffix match. A new module `src/orders/extraRoutes.js` declaring `function registerExtraRoutes(router, { store, guard })` and serving `store.list('orders')` → gate **green, exit 0**: the filename does not match, the hardcoded `routeFiles.length >= 4` floor still holds at 4, and receiving the store by parameter is not a require, so the edge rule cannot see it either. Fix: select by content (`/function register\w+Routes\(/`) and drop the magic floor. Today's four route files are all exactly `routes.js`, so nothing is missed at head.

## 5. Did the last rework weaken anything, or add unsanctioned behaviour?

**Yes, once:** the architecture gate's effective scope. At `8a96e1f` the scan read raw source, so the requires in N1's two scenarios were visible; at `f1ead20` they are not. One real false-fail (comments) was closed and one silent false-negative was opened, undeclared. The selector change is a second, marginal narrowing (N3).

The money change is otherwise a strict improvement: no value accepted now is forbidden by README, and nothing in the plausible range is newly rejected. No other `src/` file changed in the last rework (`git diff 8a96e1f f1ead20` touches `PR.md`, `src/lib/money.js`, and three test files only).

**No behaviour outside README's sanction entered.** Two unsanctioned behaviours exist and are both pre-existing and unchanged from base `2325850`: the pre-auth 405/400 (F8, recorded for the human) and `orders.cancel` going through `getOwned`, whose admin exemption lets an admin cancel an order although README grants admins read access and names the cancel caller "customer" (`src/orders/service.js:51-55,78`; identical at base — out of this diff's scope, worth a separate issue).

Verification commands I ran (three, all against a throwaway copy of the clean work tree at `f1ead20`, in `$TMPDIR` directories created and removed by the same invocation; no repository file was modified, no worktree created):

1. `node <tmp>/probe.js` (money domain probe) — exit **0**, commit `f1ead20`.
2. planted-mutation sweep, each step `node --test test/architecture.test.js` in a copy — exits **0 / 1 / 0 / 0 / 0** for baseline / string-`require(name)` / `'/*'`-bracketed require / `//`-string-prefixed require / `extraRoutes.js`, commit `f1ead20`.
3. negative control, `printf "const store = require('../store/memoryStore');" >> src/users/routes.js && node --test test/architecture.test.js` — exit **1**, commit `f1ead20`.

## What I found

The final head `f1ead20` fixes the money domain and the token-mechanism gap as claimed: all twelve command criteria passed at that commit on recorded evidence, F1–F7 and F9–F13 are resolved, and F8's non-fix is defensible. But the last rework's fix for the architecture scan (F3/F10) strips comments without modelling string literals, which **silently hides a real forbidden dependency** — I proved a `require('../store/memoryStore')` in `src/users/routes.js` goes green when bracketed by the string literals `'/*'` and `'*/'`, or placed after a string containing `//`, while the identical require is red without them.

## Why it matters

The branch's only architectural enforcement can now pass over the exact edge it exists to stop, and the trigger is ordinary code (a glob such as `'orders/*'`, a protocol-relative URL) rather than an attack; there is no CI and no negative control, so the loss would never be noticed. Acting means one rule-level change — strip string literals before comments — which also closes the remaining false-fail; not acting leaves a gate whose declared scope ("comments are stripped") is wider than its effective scope.

## 3. Attack on `fromCents(toCents(v)) === v`

**Accepts nothing README forbids.** The rule accepts `v` only when `v === fl(C/100)` for an in-range integer `C`, i.e. `v` is exactly the canonical double of a two-decimal decimal. `1.234`, `0.005`, `0.125`, `0.1+0.2`, `0.07*3` and `1.1+2.2` are all rejected (step C). The **1-cent floor is exactly right**: the smallest positive two-decimal value is `0.01`, which is accepted, and everything below rounds to 0 cents and is rejected. The **ceiling** rejects two-decimal values above 9.007e13, which README's literal text permits; PR.md discloses that as a product question — fair.

**Rejects values README permits, below the declared ceiling.** `fl(·/100)` stops being injective once cent counts exceed 2^51, so `Math.round(v*100)` can land one cent off the decimal the client sent, and the round trip then fails. Measured: **40 of 700** sampled legal two-decimal amounts in [3.5e13, 9.007e13] are rejected, e.g. `35184372088832.02` → `POST /orders` 400 "unitPrice must be a positive amount with at most two decimals" (**N4**, minor; `src/lib/money.js:16-24`). PR.md:174 says rejection starts "above about 9.007e13" — wrong by a factor of ~2.5.

**Worse in the same band: a reachable order whose stated total can never be paid (N5**, minor; `src/orders/service.js:31-39` + `src/payments/service.js:17`). `unitPrice: 35184372088832.05, quantity: 2` passes `isAmount`, sums to 7036874417766410 cents — a safe integer, so the `Number.isSafeInteger` guard does not fire — and stores `total: 70368744177664.1`. A payment of exactly that total computes `toCents` = 7036874417766409 ≠ 7036874417766410 → 400 forever. That is defect 4's own symptom ("an order that could never be paid at its own stated total") reinstated at the top of the range, and it makes PR.md:30's claim that creation "rejects a summed total that is no longer an exact cent count" incomplete. One-line fix: `if (toCents(fromCents(cents)) !== cents) throw invalid(...)`, or bound the domain at 2^51 cents where the round trip is provably injective. I rate N4/N5 minor on exposure (unit prices of ~3.5e13 currency units); if the human treats the top of the range as in scope — as F6 was — N5 is F6's class and would be major.

**Rejecting `0.1 + 0.2` does not break a legitimate client at plausible magnitudes**, and nothing in 0.01–2000.00 is rejected. Order totals now come from `fromCents`, so a client that echoes back the total it was given always passes. The real change: a client that computes an amount itself by float addition (`0.1+0.1+0.1` → `0.30000000000000004`) now gets 400 where it previously got a silent round to 0.30. README sanctions that (the number has 17 decimals), and failing loud is correct — but it is a client-visible break that PR.md's limitations do not list.

## 4. Attack on the comment stripping and the route selector

**N1 — major — `test/architecture.test.js:41-45`: the stripper does not model string literals, so it hides real dependencies.** `code()` treats any `/*` … `*/` as a comment and any `//` not preceded by `:` as a line comment, wherever they occur.

- `const GLOB = '/*'; const store = require('../store/memoryStore'); const END = '*/';` in `src/users/routes.js` → gate **green, exit 0**, while the identical require without the two string literals is **red, exit 1** (`forbidden dependency: src/users/routes.js -> src/store/memoryStore.js`).
- `const U = '//cdn'; const store = require('../store/memoryStore');` on one line → gate **green, exit 0**.
- A single unmatched `/*` inside a string (a glob such as `'orders/*'`) deletes everything to the next `*/` or to EOF, so **every** require in that file disappears and `every require target exists` passes trivially.
- At head nothing triggers it: the only `//`-in-string in `src/` is `'http://localhost'` (`src/http/router.js:37`), which the `[^:]` guard protects, and no `/*` appears in `src/` at all. The code is correct; the gate protecting it is narrower than PR.md declares. Per `gate-lifecycle` §4 this is an undeclared scope delta → `RESTORE`.
- Code following `*/` on the same line survives (the replacement is per-comment, not per-line), so that attack line finds nothing.

**N2 — minor — the gate can still fail on correct code, and PR.md says it cannot.** `const HINT = 'never use import(x) or require(name) in a message';` in `src/lib/errors.js` → **exit 1**, `src/lib/errors.js has a non-literal require: require(name)`. PR.md:130 lists "a string containing `import(`" among the twelve fixed findings; only the comment case was fixed. Same root cause and same one-line fix as N1 (blank quoted literals, then strip comments). Together with the misstated rejection boundary (N4) and the incomplete defect-8 claim (N5), this is the third consecutive round in which PR.md's claims outrun the code — `related_to: F1, F2, F11`.

**N3 — minor — `test/architecture.test.js:97-98`: the route-module selector misses route modules.** `basename().startsWith('routes.')` gains `.cjs`/`.mjs` and loses the (lowercase-only) `*routes.js` suffix match. A new module `src/orders/extraRoutes.js` declaring `function registerExtraRoutes(router, { store, guard })` and serving `store.list('orders')` → gate **green, exit 0**: the filename does not match, the hardcoded `routeFiles.length >= 4` floor still holds at 4, and receiving the store by parameter is not a require, so the edge rule cannot see it either. Fix: select by content (`/function register\w+Routes\(/`) and drop the magic floor. Today's four route files are all exactly `routes.js`, so nothing is missed at head.

**Yes, once:** the architecture gate's effective scope. At `8a96e1f` the scan read raw source, so the requires in N1's two scenarios were visible; at `f1ead20` they are not. One real false-fail (comments) was closed and one silent false-negative was opened, undeclared. The selector change is a second, marginal narrowing (N3).

The final head `f1ead20` fixes the money domain and the token-mechanism gap as claimed: all twelve command criteria passed at that commit on recorded evidence, F1–F7 and F9–F13 are resolved, and F8's non-fix is defensible. The branch's only architectural enforcement can now pass over the exact edge it exists to stop, and the trigger is ordinary code (a glob such as `'orders/*'`, a protocol-relative URL) rather than an attack; there is no CI and no negative control, so the loss would never be noticed. Acting means one rule-level change — strip string literals before comments — which also closes the remaining false-fail; not acting leaves a gate whose declared scope ("comments are stripped") is wider than its effective scope.

## 3. Attack on `fromCents(toCents(v)) === v`

**Accepts nothing README forbids.** The rule accepts `v` only when `v === fl(C/100)` for an in-range integer `C`, i.e. `v` is exactly the canonical double of a two-decimal decimal. `1.234`, `0.005`, `0.125`, `0.1+0.2`, `0.07*3` and `1.1+2.2` are all rejected (step C). The **1-cent floor is exactly right**: the smallest positive two-decimal value is `0.01`, which is accepted, and everything below rounds to 0 cents and is rejected. The **ceiling** rejects two-decimal values above 9.007e13, which README's literal text permits; PR.md discloses that as a product question — fair.

**Rejects values README permits, below the declared ceiling.** `fl(·/100)` stops being injective once cent counts exceed 2^51, so `Math.round(v*100)` can land one cent off the decimal the client sent, and the round trip then fails. Measured: **40 of 700** sampled legal two-decimal amounts in [3.5e13, 9.007e13] are rejected, e.g. `35184372088832.02` → `POST /orders` 400 "unitPrice must be a positive amount with at most two decimals" (**N4**, minor; `src/lib/money.js:16-24`). PR.md:174 says rejection starts "above about 9.007e13" — wrong by a factor of ~2.5.

**Worse in the same band: a reachable order whose stated total can never be paid (N5**, minor; `src/orders/service.js:31-39` + `src/payments/service.js:17`). `unitPrice: 35184372088832.05, quantity: 2` passes `isAmount`, sums to 7036874417766410 cents — a safe integer, so the `Number.isSafeInteger` guard does not fire — and stores `total: 70368744177664.1`. A payment of exactly that total computes `toCents` = 7036874417766409 ≠ 7036874417766410 → 400 forever. That is defect 4's own symptom ("an order that could never be paid at its own stated total") reinstated at the top of the range, and it makes PR.md:30's claim that creation "rejects a summed total that is no longer an exact cent count" incomplete. One-line fix: `if (toCents(fromCents(cents)) !== cents) throw invalid(...)`, or bound the domain at 2^51 cents where the round trip is provably injective. I rate N4/N5 minor on exposure (unit prices of ~3.5e13 currency units); if the human treats the top of the range as in scope — as F6 was — N5 is F6's class and would be major.

**Rejecting `0.1 + 0.2` does not break a legitimate client at plausible magnitudes**, and nothing in 0.01–2000.00 is rejected. Order totals now come from `fromCents`, so a client that echoes back the total it was given always passes. The real change: a client that computes an amount itself by float addition (`0.1+0.1+0.1` → `0.30000000000000004`) now gets 400 where it previously got a silent round to 0.30. README sanctions that (the number has 17 decimals), and failing loud is correct — but it is a client-visible break that PR.md's limitations do not list.

## 4. Attack on the comment stripping and the route selector

**N1 — major — `test/architecture.test.js:41-45`: the stripper does not model string literals, so it hides real dependencies.** `code()` treats any `/*` … `*/` as a comment and any `//` not preceded by `:` as a line comment, wherever they occur.

- `const GLOB = '/*'; const store = require('../store/memoryStore'); const END = '*/';` in `src/users/routes.js` → gate **green, exit 0**, while the identical require without the two string literals is **red, exit 1** (`forbidden dependency: src/users/routes.js -> src/store/memoryStore.js`).
- `const U = '//cdn'; const store = require('../store/memoryStore');` on one line → gate **green, exit 0**.
- A single unmatched `/*` inside a string (a glob such as `'orders/*'`) deletes everything to the next `*/` or to EOF, so **every** require in that file disappears and `every require target exists` passes trivially.
- At head nothing triggers it: the only `//`-in-string in `src/` is `'http://localhost'` (`src/http/router.js:37`), which the `[^:]` guard protects, and no `/*` appears in `src/` at all. The code is correct; the gate protecting it is narrower than PR.md declares. Per `gate-lifecycle` §4 this is an undeclared scope delta → `RESTORE`.
- Code following `*/` on the same line survives (the replacement is per-comment, not per-line), so that attack line finds nothing.

**N2 — minor — the gate can still fail on correct code, and PR.md says it cannot.** `const HINT = 'never use import(x) or require(name) in a message';` in `src/lib/errors.js` → **exit 1**, `src/lib/errors.js has a non-literal require: require(name)`. PR.md:130 lists "a string containing `import(`" among the twelve fixed findings; only the comment case was fixed. Same root cause and same one-line fix as N1 (blank quoted literals, then strip comments). Together with the misstated rejection boundary (N4) and the incomplete defect-8 claim (N5), this is the third consecutive round in which PR.md's claims outrun the code — `related_to: F1, F2, F11`.

**N3 — minor — `test/architecture.test.js:97-98`: the route-module selector misses route modules.** `basename().startsWith('routes.')` gains `.cjs`/`.mjs` and loses the (lowercase-only) `*routes.js` suffix match. A new module `src/orders/extraRoutes.js` declaring `function registerExtraRoutes(router, { store, guard })` and serving `store.list('orders')` → gate **green, exit 0**: the filename does not match, the hardcoded `routeFiles.length >= 4` floor still holds at 4, and receiving the store by parameter is not a require, so the edge rule cannot see it either. Fix: select by content (`/function register\w+Routes\(/`) and drop the magic floor. Today's four route files are all exactly `routes.js`, so nothing is missed at head.

  module taking the store would pass.
